summary: Inspect a supplied Enhanced CT object through shared/per-frame functional groups and dimension-index presentation while preserving original one-based frame identity.
objective: Inspect a supplied Enhanced CT object through shared/per-frame functional groups and dimension-index presentation while preserving original one-based frame identity.
example_prompts: Build enhanced dicom acquisition-frame inspector with explicit provenance, laterality, frame and unavailable-state checks.
negative_signals: infer missing clinical data from geometry
not_for: Diagnosis, treatment, procedure guidance or patient-specific inference.

entities.name: Frame ledger
entities.guidance: List SOP Instance UID, original frame number and dimension-index values separately from presentation order.

entities.name: Functional groups
entities.guidance: Show whether a selected value came from Shared or its matching Per-Frame item.

entities.name: Derived plane card
entities.guidance: Place only frames with valid position/orientation in patient coordinates; otherwise retain metadata-only state.

state_contract.model: Accept an authorized/de-identified supplied multiframe instance with NumberOfFrames>=1. Preserve source order. Resolve the single Shared Functional Groups item, which may be empty. The Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence may be absent when all per-frame groups are empty; when present it has one item per frame, individual items may be empty, and its count equals NumberOfFrames. A functional-group macro cannot occur in both Shared and Per-Frame. Follow Dimension Index pointers rather than assuming z or time.
state_contract.authority: Supplied source records, identifiers, frames and curated labels own state. Blender/glTF geometry is display-only; Three.js owns validated runtime binding and exact reset.

invariants: A functional-group macro is resolved from Shared or Per-Frame, never both; absent or empty conditional groups remain explicit.
First dimension is slowest-varying presentation guidance, not automatically anatomy or time.
No patient identifiers enter glTF, screenshots or fixtures.
motion_guidance: Scrubbing changes only selected source frame and derived display plane: Blender exports a generic card/axes shell with no instance pixels or patient metadata, while Three.js retains one-based source identity, resolves conditional Shared/Per-Frame metadata and drives planes only when source orientation/position is valid.
creative_affordances: Use restrained cutaways, translucent planes and non-color selection cues without implying clinical confidence.
known_limits: Documentary source review only; no dataset, patient record, simulation, specialist clinical validation or runtime was used.

claims.statement: DICOM PS3.3 specifies one Shared Functional Groups item that may be empty. Per-Frame Functional Groups is conditional: it is required if any frame has a nonempty per-frame group and, when present, has one possibly empty item per frame. A functional-group macro cannot occur in both sequences. Dimension pointers and values organize presentation, with the first dimension slowest-varying.
claims.scope: DICOM PS3.3 2026c C.7.6.16, C.7.6.17 and 7.5.2; meaning follows the referenced macro/IOD.

object_craft.structure: Blender authors one generic unit plane card, axes and neutral panel at identity; glTF exports only these reusable display assets, with no instance pixels, UIDs or patient metadata.
object_craft.material: Neutral cards distinguish source/shared/per-frame state without medical heat-map semantics.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js owns authorized frame records, conditional Shared/Per-Frame resolution, one-based identity, source-to-presentation ordering, patient-frame plane transforms and scrub/reset state.

physical_contract.scope: Display of supplied educational or derived biomedical records; no tissue mechanics or diagnostic model.
checks: Reject ambiguous side, unit or frame.
